findings.title: Cleanup service ticker interval unintentionally reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This appears to be leftover debugging code: it causes all background cleanup jobs (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, expired images, user invites, short URLs, and query history) to run 10x more frequently than intended and conflicts with the 9-minute timeout configured in `clean()`.

findings.title: Leftover debug statements log at Error level and dump all batch IDs on every iteration
findings.body: `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` call `r.log.Error` twice per batch iteration (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579) even when operations succeed and `err` is `nil`. Additionally, lines 534, 554, and 576 serialize the full `ids` slice into the error log on every batch, flooding production error logs during normal cleanup runs.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when constructing SQLite IN clause for large batches
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the comma-separated ID list is constructed in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. Because this only runs for batch sizes above 999, the repeated string copying is O(N^2) in both CPU and memory (for a batch of 32,767 IDs as in the test, a single batch allocates multiple gigabytes of temporary strings). A `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` buffer should be used instead.
